name: Meghalaya
tagline: Cascading Waterfalls, Crystal Rivers & Living Root Bridges
heroCaption: Nohkalikai Falls plunging 1,115 ft into a turquoise pool, Cherrapunji
summary: Explore the Khasi and Jaintia Hills from Guwahati on smooth four-lane mountain highways. Witness Nohkalikai Falls in Cherrapunji, glide along the crystal-clear Umngot River in Dawki, and trek to century-old Living Root Bridges woven from native Ficus elastica trees.

bestSeason.months: October to April (Dry & Clear) / June to September (Monsoon Roar)
bestSeason.waterClarity: Peak water clarity at Umngot River Dawki from November to April.
bestSeason.waterfalls: Most thunderous and lush during monsoon from June to September.
bestSeason.tradeoffs: Winter is crisp and sunny, but water volume at smaller waterfalls drops. Monsoon offers roaring cascades, but river boating in Dawki is restricted.

routeFromGuwahati.distance: 100 km to Shillong / 155 km to Cherrapunji
routeFromGuwahati.driveTime: 3 to 4 hours on smooth 4-lane mountain highway (NH6)
routeFromGuwahati.pickupPoint: Guwahati Airport (GAU) or Guwahati Railway Station (GHY)

permitNotes: No special permits or Inner Line Permits (ILP) required for Indian or foreign nationals visiting Meghalaya.

highlights.title: Nohkalikai & Wei Sawdong Falls
highlights.description: Dramatic 1,115-ft cliffside plunge and the three-tiered emerald forest pools of Sohra.
highlights.caption: Nohkalikai Falls viewpoint overlooking the southern Bangladesh plains

highlights.title: Double Decker Living Root Bridge
highlights.description: Century-old living botanical bridges in Nongriat valley, maintained by indigenous Khasi villagers.
highlights.image: /images/Meghalaya/Cherrapunjee/Double Decker Root Bridge/Double Decker Root Bridge.jpg
highlights.caption: Double Decker Root Bridge spanning the rainforest river at Nongriat

highlights.title: Umngot River Dawki
highlights.description: Glass-like emerald river near the border where wooden country boats appear suspended in air.
highlights.caption: Crystal-clear waters of Umngot River during the autumn and winter season

highlights.title: Mawlynnong & Riwai
highlights.description: Community-maintained village in East Khasi Hills famous for living root walkways and flower-lined lanes.

highlights.title: Krang Suri Falls & Laitlum Canyons
highlights.description: Electric-blue cascade in the Jaintia Hills and dramatic sweeping canyon gorges at Laitlum.

faqs.q: How many days are ideal for a complete Meghalaya tour?
faqs.a: A 5-day itinerary covers Shillong, Cherrapunji, Dawki, and Mawlynnong comfortably. Adding offbeat Jaintia hills or Shnongpdeng camping requires 6 to 7 days.

faqs.q: Can elders and children visit the Living Root Bridges?
faqs.a: The single living root bridge at Riwai (near Mawlynnong) requires only an easy 10-minute flat walk accessible to everyone. The Double Decker at Nongriat involves 3,500 stone stairs and is recommended for active walkers.

name: Arunachal Pradesh
tagline: High Himalayan Passes, Ancient Monasteries & Monpa Heritage
heroCaption: Welcome Gateway to Tawang at Sela Pass (13,700 ft) under fresh snow
summary: Traverse the Eastern Himalayas from subtropical river valleys to 13,700-ft Sela Pass. Visit the 400-year-old Galden Namgyal Lhatse monastery in Tawang, cross high alpine glacial lakes, and experience indigenous Monpa mountain hospitality.

bestSeason.months: March to May (Spring blooms) & October to December (Clear skies & snow)
bestSeason.waterClarity: Glacial streams run crystal clear in autumn and winter.
bestSeason.waterfalls: Nuranang (Jang) Falls roars at peak capacity through summer and autumn.
bestSeason.tradeoffs: Winter (Dec to Feb) can see temporary snowfall delays at Sela Pass. Experienced mountain drivers with 4x4 or snow-chain experience are essential.

routeFromGuwahati.distance: 450 km to Tawang via Bhalukpong and Dirang
routeFromGuwahati.driveTime: Traversed over 2 days with overnight halt at Bhalukpong or Dirang Valley

permitNotes: Mandatory Inner Line Permit (ILP) required for all Indian domestic tourists. Protected Area Permit (PAP) required for foreign nationals. We coordinate all permit clearances on your behalf.

highlights.title: Sela Pass & Sela Lake (13,700 ft)
highlights.description: High-altitude Himalayan gateway connecting West Kameng to Tawang, framed by frozen Sela Lake and Buddhist prayer flags.
highlights.caption: Iconic Welcome to Tawang Gateway at Sela Pass under fresh snow

highlights.title: Tawang Monastery
highlights.description: Asia's second-largest Buddhist monastery, perched like a fortress at 10,000 ft overlooking the Tawang valley.
highlights.caption: The historic 400-year-old Tawang Monastery complex

highlights.title: Dirang Valley & Monpa Community Heritage
highlights.description: Peaceful river valley homestays offering cultural interaction with the indigenous Monpa community in their traditional handwoven attire.
highlights.caption: Monpa community gathering in traditional mountain dress, Western Arunachal

highlights.title: Bum La Pass & Sangetsar Lake
highlights.description: High-altitude Indo-China border post at 15,200 ft and the famous Sangetsar (Madhuri) Lake ringed by dead tree trunks.

highlights.title: Jaswant Garh & Nuranang Falls
highlights.description: Historic 1962 war memorial and the roaring 100-meter Jang waterfall located between Sela Pass and Tawang.

faqs.q: How do we get an Inner Line Permit (ILP) for Arunachal?
faqs.a: Simply share your government photo ID and passport-size photo with our team during booking. We obtain the verified government ILP before your journey begins.

faqs.q: Can we take our Guwahati rental car all the way to Bum La Pass?
faqs.a: Per local district rules in Tawang, excursions to Bum La Pass and Sangetsar Lake must be operated by authorized local Tawang taxi union 4x4 vehicles. We coordinate this seamless changeover for you.

name: Assam
tagline: One-Horned Rhinoceros Safaris, Brahmaputra Cruises & Heritage Tea
heroCaption: Wild One-Horned Rhinoceros in Kaziranga National Park grasslands
summary: Home to two-thirds of the world's Great One-Horned Rhinoceros population in Kaziranga National Park. Travel from Guwahati through emerald tea estates, cruise the Brahmaputra River at sunset, and visit the historic Kamakhya temple.

bestSeason.waterClarity: Brahmaputra cruises are tranquil from November through March.
bestSeason.waterfalls: Explore tea gardens in blooming harvest season from April through November.
bestSeason.tradeoffs: Kaziranga National Park is closed to safaris during the monsoon season (June to late September) due to annual river flooding.

routeFromGuwahati.distance: Guwahati city / 220 km to Kaziranga National Park
routeFromGuwahati.driveTime: 4 to 4.5 hours on scenic four-lane Asian Highway 1 (AH1)

permitNotes: No special border permits required for Assam. Safari tickets and wildlife forest entries are booked through authorized park counters.

highlights.title: Kaziranga Jeep Safaris
highlights.description: Open-top 4x4 game drives in Bagori and Kohora ranges spotting rhinos, elephants, wild water buffalo, and swamp deer.

highlights.title: Maa Kamakhya Temple
highlights.description: Ancient hilltop Shakti Peetha shrine atop Nilachal Hill offering sweeping views across Guwahati and the river.

highlights.title: Sunset Brahmaputra River Cruise
highlights.description: Evening river vessel cruise with traditional folk music and golden-hour sunset views across the Brahmaputra.

highlights.title: Heritage Assam Tea Estates
highlights.description: Walk amidst manicured tea gardens and observe traditional orthodox tea processing.

highlights.title: Umananda Island (Peacock Island)
highlights.description: Smallest inhabited river island in the world housing an ancient Shiva shrine, reached by a quick country ferry.

faqs.q: Which safari zone in Kaziranga is best for seeing rhinos?
faqs.a: The Western (Bagori) zone has the highest density of one-horned rhinos, while the Central (Kohora) zone is renowned for wetlands and water birds.

faqs.q: How do we arrange VIP passes for Kamakhya Temple?
faqs.a: Special VIP darshan entry passes (approx ₹500 per person) are issued directly by the temple administration on the spot. Your driver guides you directly to the counter.

name: Dzukou Valley Trek
tagline: High-Altitude Rolling Bamboo Meadows on the Nagaland Frontier
heroCaption: Serpentine crystal streams and rolling bamboo ridges of Dzukou Valley at 8,000 ft
summary: A high-altitude hiking sanctuary situated at 8,000 feet on the Nagaland and Manipur border. Famous for its undulating dwarf bamboo ridges, cold mountain streams, natural rock caves, and seasonal alpine flora.

bestSeason.months: June to August (Dzukou Lily bloom) / October to March (Clear skies & frost)
bestSeason.waterClarity: Pristine potable mountain streams run crystal clear inside the valley floor.
bestSeason.waterfalls: Misty gorges and lush moss throughout the summer months.
bestSeason.tradeoffs: Monsoon trek requires rain ponchos and leech socks. Winter nights drop below freezing (0°C), requiring heavy thermal gear.

routeFromGuwahati.distance: Guwahati to Dimapur (train/road, 4-5 hrs) then 3 hrs drive to Kigwema trailhead
routeFromGuwahati.driveTime: Trailhead to valley rim: 4 to 5 hours moderate uphill hike
routeFromGuwahati.pickupPoint: Dimapur Airport / Railway Station or Guwahati transfer

permitNotes: Domestic tourists require a Nagaland Inner Line Permit (ILP), easily processed online. Trail entry fees and community sanitation levies are paid at the Viswema / Jakhama checkpost.

highlights.title: Rolling Emerald Ridges
highlights.description: Undulating dwarf bamboo hillocks that transition from emerald green in summer to golden frost in winter.

highlights.title: Campsite Stargazing
highlights.description: Zero light pollution gives you the full brilliance of the Milky Way arching over the valley rim.

highlights.title: Crystal Streams & Rock Caves
highlights.description: Natural rock overhangs, cold-water plunge pools, and ancient shepherd caves along the valley floor.

highlights.title: Angami Naga Trail Hospitality
highlights.description: Trail stewardship and rest house management by the Southern Angami Youth Organisation (SAYO).

highlights.title: Historic Kohima & Kisama
highlights.description: World War II memorial and the traditional tribal architecture of Kisama Heritage Village.

faqs.q: How physically demanding is the Dzukou Valley trek?
faqs.a: The first 1.5 to 2 hours from Viswema involve steep stone stairs through forest. Once you crest the ridge, the walk into the valley rest house is gentle and flat. Anyone with basic fitness can complete it.

faqs.q: What accommodation is available inside the valley?
faqs.a: The valley features the SAYO Community Rest House with basic shared dormitories and wooden plank floors. We also provide alpine tents and insulated mats for campers.
